symptom: `create or modify navigation` (or `create or replace`, deprecated or `mdl 1` spelling) naming a home page, role home, login page, not-found page or a menu item's page/microflow/nanoflow that does not exist passed `check -p` ("Check passed!") and `exec` ("Navigation profile 'Responsive' updated."); only `mx check` objected: CE1613 "The selected page 'Shop.NoSuchHome' no longer exists." at Navigation profile, and one per bad menu item. A page's own show page / call microflow and an unknown icon were refused. Same for `create menu`.
cause: The reference-resolution passes were added one reference kind at a time (validateWidgetReferences for widget trees, validateIconRefs, validateNavigationRoles for the role only), so navigation targets were in none of them. The exec handler built each menu action with a pageBuilder whose tolerateDanglingRefs is true for menus (so a target stored by name never failed), and read home/login/not-found pages straight into the spec; CREATE OR REPLACE NAVIGATION rewrites the whole profile.
file: `mdl/executor/validate_navigation_targets.go` (`navigationTargets`, `unresolvedNavigationTargets`, `validateNavigationTargets` called from `validateProgramWithWarnings`; `validateNavigationTargetsForExec` called first in `execAlterNavigation` and `execCreateMenu`); forward references via `navigationDefRefs` in `eagerDefRefs` and `Executor.enterScriptFlows` (`scriptTargets`)
insight: A reference pass written per kind leaves every kind it does not list silently unchecked, and the escape is silent both ways (check passes, exec writes, the build reports it one build later) — when adding a statement that names documents, grep every place a page/microflow name is resolved and ask which statements are NOT in the list. Navigation targets are written by a statement that replaces the whole profile, so the refusal has to come before the write, in the handler as well as in the pre-flight (`exec --no-check` skips the pre-flight). Reuse the same lookups (buildPageQualifiedNames and friends). A target stored by name and created further down the script must follow the flow-call rule (forwardFlowCalls, #1405) rather than statement order: a first version that made it an MDL-ORDER01 error broke a working script shape (navigation written before its pages: upstream execs it and mx check reports 0 errors) — measure what upstream does with the other order before enforcing one. Measured on a Mendix 11.12.5 app: 4 CE1613 before for the reported script, 0 errors after a valid navigation; an empty listing from the backend is silence, not a finding (as in validateForwardDefRefs)
